prior_production_model.description: v1: 6-feature GBM (career_avg, platoon_delta, pitcher_oba_against, park_factor, is_home, batting_order), trained/validated with a within-2025-season date split only.

prior_production_model.note: random_forest scored marginally better on this same 2026 holdout (log_loss 0.6463 vs this gbm's 0.6468) but was rejected: sklearn's RandomForestClassifier has no monotonic-constraint mechanism, and direct point-checks showed it predicting a .230 career hitter below a .200 one at otherwise-default features -- the same backwards-prediction pathology monotonic_cst was introduced to fix in the original 6-feature model. This gbm has monotonic_cst applied (see scripts/train_ml_model.py MONOTONIC_CST) and was verified by point-checks across every constrained feature before shipping.

Adds bvp_delta (batter history vs. this specific opposing pitcher, delta vs season-to-date average) to the prior 12-feature model. Found via scripts/test_bvp.py (since removed -- superseded by this production integration; see git history and README for the original finding: 94.8% of a 2000-draw bootstrap favored including it, no obvious confound mechanism unlike the rejected bullpen-quality feature). Verified monotonic (non-decreasing in bvp_delta) by point-check before shipping.

bvp_delta is now thresholded: treated as 0 (no information) below MIN_BVP_AB=3 prior at-bats vs. the exact opposing pitcher, instead of always using the raw delta regardless of sample size. Found via scripts/test_bvp_sample_size.py after a user spotted a 2-for-2 showing up as "has hit this pitcher well historically" on the live site -- a real number from too small a sample to support that claim. Tested 6 candidates (hard thresholds at 3/5/10 AB, shrinkage at C=5/10/20): a light threshold (>=3 AB) was the best of all of them (log_loss 0.6470 -> 0.6469, 82% of a 2000-draw bootstrap favoring it); heavier thresholds (5, 10 AB) scored WORSE than the unthresholded version, meaning real signal exists in the 3-9 AB range that an aggressive cutoff would throw away. Verified monotonic (conditionally, like platoon_delta) by point-check before shipping.

Follow-up to the bvp_delta sample-size fix: audited every other fractional feature for the same problem (scripts/test_sample_size_audit.py). pitcher_oba_against (season-to-date, min 3 AB faced), career_avg, and career_obp all showed real, validated improvement from empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward league average (shrunk = raw*w + league_avg*(1-w), w=n/(n+C)): C=25/600/100 respectively. Combined bootstrap vs the fully-raw version: log_loss 0.6468 -> 0.6467, 67% of a 2000-draw bootstrap favoring the shrunk version. Verified monotonic by point-check before shipping. career_k_rate, career_bb_rate, pitcher_era_career, and pitcher_k9_career were tested the same way and shrinkage measurably HURT them at every strength tried -- left raw, deliberately.

metadata.note: Recency weighting for career_k_rate: prior seasons weighted by 0.5**(seasons_ago) before summing strikeouts/PA, instead of every prior season counting equally (scripts/test_recency_weighting.py). Motivated by the sample-size shrinkage audit finding that shrinkage toward league average actively HURT career_k_rate/career_bb_rate/pitcher_era_career/pitcher_k9_career (round five) -- those features needed a different correction: recency weighting asks whether data from 5 years ago is as informative as last year, which shrinkage cannot express. career_k_rate alone: log_loss 0.6467->0.6465, 82.7% of a 1500-draw paired bootstrap favoring. pitcher_era_career and pitcher_k9_career ALSO individually improved with recency weighting (69.8%/63.6%) but combining any 2+ of the three features together was worse than any single one alone -- pairing pitcher_era_career with pitcher_k9_career specifically was actively harmful (0.8% favoring), since both derive from the same outs count and double-weighting gives the GBM two correlated-but-not-identical signals its splits handle worse than one clean one (scripts/test_recency_weighting_combos.py, all 7 subsets swept). Only career_k_rate ships with recency weighting; pitcher_era_career/pitcher_k9_career stay flat, unchanged from the prior shipped model. career_avg/career_obp/career_bb_rate were also tested for recency weighting and did not benefit -- unchanged. Monotonicity re-verified via point-check sweeps across 3 feature contexts.
